## TL;DR

Task #1258 makes three phone-polish changes: the app root opens Work instead of Mission Control, the routed page's scrollbar is hidden on phone widths, and every header-row control shares one height token. The implementation was already on the branch from earlier passes. This pass brought the branch up to date with main, confirmed the branch is clean of foreign files and `repoos.toml`, and ran the scoped gate, which passed on the remote validation host.

## Work and rationale

- **Home route.** `src/ui-app/src/router.ts` redirects `/` to `/work`. Mission Control moved to `/control`, and `nav.ts` points the Control item there. Deep links and unknown paths behave as before, and the not-found view now links to Mission Control at `/control`.
- **Scrollbar.** A phone-only block at the end of `style.css` (under 720px) hides the scrollbar on `.main > :not(.spin)` and drops the 3px right padding that `.page-scroll-body` and `.agents-tab-content` reserved for it. Touch and keyboard scrolling are unchanged because the element still scrolls. The block sits last so it wins over the base rules. Desktop keeps its bars.
- **Header row.** `--topbar-control-h` is set on `.topbar` (30px on desktop, 44px at 900px and below). The project chip, search, bell, theme, help and account controls all read it, so they share a height and centre vertically. The chip uses a 999px radius to match the search field, 13px text at weight 600 and a bold project name.
- **Docs and tests.** `home-route-work.test.ts` covers the `/` redirect and the `/control` path. `mobile-header-scroll-browser.test.ts` is a headless WebKit test that checks header heights at 375, 412, 768 and 1280px in dark and light themes, the phone gutters, and that the page still scrolls. `docs/qa/2026-11-mobile-polish-1258.md` lists what was checked and what was not. The ADR line that cited `/` for Mission Control now points to `/control`.

## Approaches tried

- For the header, I kept one token rather than matching per-control values. Several controls read it, so a later change to one of them cannot quietly desync the row.
- For the scrollbar, I scoped the hide to the routed page under the phone breakpoint instead of the whole document. That keeps any nested scrollers and desktop bars unchanged.
- I considered changing the `/` route to a component that renders Work. A redirect is cheaper and also makes the Hub's start URL land on Work without a second code path.

## Challenges and blockers

- **Stale branch base.** The branch was far behind main, and main moved again while the scoped check was running. I merged main twice. The second merge brought only `work/` bookkeeping from other tasks and had no conflicts, so the code I checked is unchanged. This is the one place I did not run a fresh check: the final merge touched only bookkeeping files.
- **`repoos.toml`.** The queued message said the branch carried a stray `repoos.toml`. In this session `git diff main -- repoos.toml` showed no difference and the worktree was clean, so I made no change to that file.
- **Foreign task files.** The earlier review flagged `work/1275`, `work/1276` and `work/1278`. After the merges, `git diff main --name-only` lists only this task's `work/reports/1258/` files and its own task file, so that finding is cleared on this branch.
- **Real device not verified.** The Android Hub and a real phone were not tested. Touch feel, the phone's own overlay scrollbar, and the Hub's start URL are unconfirmed. A person needs to check those on a device. Headless WebKit draws overlay bars, so the scrollbar-hiding rule is pinned by a stylesheet test rather than measured.

## Key learnings

- Check `git diff main --name-only` before handoff, not only the code diff. A branch that was merged with an old main carries other tasks' bookkeeping, and that trips the scope check even when the code is right.
- A header height expressed as one token is simpler to keep consistent than matching several per-control values.
- Verify each claim against the log you ran. The remote validation result in the gate log is the evidence for this pass; the per-file test counts come from that same log.
